transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-27
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Mirage InfoSec), Samir (Procurement), Ava (Platform)

Summary (auto): quick triage of Mirage's security questionnaire (SIG/CAIQ), map high-priority evidence needs, discuss SSO/RBAC options, KMS and data residency constraints, and agree next steps for SOC 2 and a short POC.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. can you all hear me ok?
[00:06] Jordan (Mirage InfoSec): yep, i'm good. thanks for setting this up. we've got about an hour; we'll try to stick to the high-priority SIG items.
[00:15] Priya (Redwood SE): hi folks. quick intros - i'm priya, i'm on the solutions side, i'll own the technical mapping. alex will cover contract and evidence flow.
[00:22] Samir (Procurement): thanks. i'll keep an eye on timelines. we've got a procurement checkpoint on sept 15.
[00:30] Alex: perfect. jordan, maybe start with the top 3 must-haves from your side?
[00:34] Jordan: sure. first, data residency - we need EU-only processing for eu customers. second, KMS control, customer-managed keys ideally. third, audit logs retention at least 12 months and an easy export.
[00:48] Priya: cool. so that maps to Redwood Private - our VPC option supports region pinning, and we do have on-prem packages for full physical isolation. for KMS we integrate with customer KMS via envelope encryption and can support both cloud KMS and on-prem HSMs.
[01:05] Ava (Platform Eng): sorry to interrupt - can you clarify "envelope encryption" in practice? our security team prefers no plaintext in any customer-managed keys.
[01:12] Priya: yeah, good question. our model runtime uses a data encryption key per-tenant which is wrapped by the customer KMS key. plaintext keys are never stored in the control plane. we can produce a short tech note.
[01:26] Jordan: good. please also note we need key rotation policies documented and proof of rotation.
[01:33] Alex: we have a rotation schedule section in the KMS evidence pack, we can share that plus logs showing rotation events — that's included in SOC2 artefacts. we'll attach later.
[01:42] Samir: about audit logs - is there a SIEM integration or just exports?
[01:47] Priya: exports via secure streaming S3 or direct syslog integration to customer SIEM; we also have an API to pull events. retention is configurable per deployment.
[01:56] Jordan: ok, make a note - we want to see example logs with user principals and RBAC actions.
[02:03] Priya: noted. we'll include a sample with obfuscated identifiers.
[02:10] Alex: moving to SIG/CAIQ — jordan sent over a long spreadsheet. our plan is to triage and flag high-risk rows first. priya can you walk through the mapping approach?
[02:20] Priya: yeah. we typically produce a CAIQ mapping doc where each question maps to a Redwood artifact — SOC 2 control, ISO clause, or architecture diagram. for ambiguous items, we mark them "requires evidence". for example, questions about multi-tenant isolation map to our deployment model doc and the tenancy architecture.
[02:39] Jordan: that's fine. a couple of the SIG entries ask about 'runtime key management' and the wording is weird, sometimes they write K-V cache or KV cache, it's a bit messy.
[02:47] Priya: haha, yes transcription errors. but for runtime keys we can show how the KV cache never persists keys to disk and how we purge the in-memory cache on model unload. we can produce flow diagrams.
[03:01] Unknown - Speaker 4: uh hi? sorry i was muted earlier, this is Mike from Mirage infra. on multitenancy, do you do hardware isolation per-customer?
[03:09] Priya: we have options. hosted: logical multi-tenant with strict namespace isolation, dedicated: single-tenant GPU pools, and private: fully customer-managed infra. if you require physical separation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[03:23] Jordan: pricing aside, for Regulated EU customers we need dedicated pools or private, yes. can you provide a delta on latency/cost between hosted and dedicated?
[03:34] Priya: quick numbers - on our workload, hosted is lower commit cost but higher noisy neighbor risk; dedicated gives predictable P99 latencies and consistent throughput. i'll send a short perf sheet based on your QPS numbers if ava can share them.
[03:47] Ava: i'll share expected QPS and average sequence length after this call, thanks.
[03:52] Alex: moving on - SSO and RBAC. jordan, do you require SAML or OIDC?
[03:58] Jordan: SAML is preferred for our corporate SSO, but OIDC is ok. we also need SCIM provisioning for user sync.
[04:05] Priya: we support SSO via SAML and OIDC, and SCIM provisioning for user/role sync. RBAC is role-based with custom roles. there are some screenshots in the admin console deck.
[04:16] Jordan: is there audit trail for role changes with who/when?
[04:20] Priya: yes, role changes are logged and included in the admin event stream; we can export those events and include them in the evidence pack.
[04:27] Samir: procurement note - we'll need a signed DPA and specific clauses on data residency. alex, are those standard?
[04:33] Alex: yes we have a DPA template with regional processing addenda; we can push the EU addendum. i'll attach the DPA to the CRM record.
[04:41] Jordan: on SOC 2, do you have a current type II and when was it last audited?
[04:46] Alex: we completed a SOC 2 type II for the period ending 2026-06-30. i'll attach the PDF and a summary sheet.
[04:55] Jordan: great. we still need specific control-level evidence for some SIG questions, like separation of duties and backup/restoration tests.
[05:03] Priya: we can provide control narratives, backup test logs, and a restoration runbook excerpt. note some redaction will be necessary for internal IP.
[05:13] Jordan: that's expected. on encryption in transit — TLS versions etc — we need cipher lists and cert management details.
[05:20] Priya: we enforce TLS1.2+ and have cert rotation via automation. we can share cipher suites and the cert automation runbook.
[05:29] Jordan: are there any third-party subprocessors we should call out?
[05:33] Alex: yes - cloud provider (GCP), logging provider (LogStream), and metrics provider (TelemetryCo). we'll add subprocessors to the DPA appendix and mark them in the SIG mapping.
[05:45] Jordan: do any of those subprocessors have EU data residency?
[05:49] Alex: GCP has EU regions, and we can constrain resources to eu-west1, etc. LogStream supports eu data residency for logs on enterprise accounts; we'll note that and provide contact doc.
[06:00] Samir: procurement question — for evidence delivery, are you comfortable uploading to our secure SFTP, or do you prefer to share via a secure docket?
[06:08] Alex: we generally use secure S3 buckets with pre-signed URLs or direct upload to a secure collection portal. if you prefer SFTP we can work that, but S3 presigned is faster.
[06:18] Jordan: note: legal prefers direct SFTP to internal controls.
[06:22] Alex: ok we'll accommodate SFTP.
[06:25] Priya: a quick callout on PII: our hosted inference option by default does not persist inputs beyond processing; customer data retention settings can be configured. we can provide flow diagrams.
[06:38] Jordan: do you do any training on customer data? like for fine-tuning using customer corpora?
[06:44] Priya: we do not use customer data to improve base models unless a customer explicitly opts into a training contract; for hosted inference we isolate requests and have settings to opt in/out. we'll include the policy doc.
[06:57] Ava: regarding the POC, what shape should we provide for sample traffic? header formats, auth tokens, etc?
[07:04] Priya: send a small corpus with typical prompts, expected tokens per request, QPS, and auth method (SAML or API key). we'll run it against a dedicated test instance.
[07:12] Jordan: timeline check - we need the SIG returned with evidence and priority flags by sept 10 to make the procurement meeting sept 15. are those deadlines doable?
[07:20] Alex: timeline is tight but feasible. we'll prioritize high-risk items and mark items that require on-prem demo.
[07:27] Samir: any legal questions around indemnity?
[07:30] Alex: legal will take the DPA and standard terms; we can escalate indemnity items if needed.
[07:36] Jordan: one more — audit logs: can you show user principals tied back to SSO identity? that's important for us.
[07:42] Priya: yes, our logs include SSO principal id fields. we'll provide a sanitized sample export.
[07:49] Unknown - Speaker 4 (Mike): also, can you show proof of pen tests and frequency?
[07:54] Alex: we do annual external pentests and quarterly internal scans. we can share the high-level summary and remediation timelines; full reports are redacted.
[08:05] Jordan: ok, sounds good.
[08:07] Priya: quick note — for CAIQ we will usually mark "implemented" or "partially implemented" and attach the evidence link. sometimes customers want us to self-host artifacts in their environment; that's a Private deployment conversation.
[08:19] Ava: on cost for private, can you send a range? we need it for TCO.
[08:24] Alex: yes, priya will follow up with a ballpark. again depends on GPU types and commit.
[08:31] Jordan: last item — retention of evidence. once you upload the artifacts to our SFTP, how long will Redwood keep copies?
[08:39] Alex: we typically keep an evidence snapshot for the duration of the sales process and 90 days after close unless otherwise agreed in the DPA. we can change that per contract.
[08:50] Samir: ok.
[08:52] Alex: let's recap next steps - i'll send SOC2 + KMS rotation note + DPA template; priya will run the POC and produce CAIQ mapping; ava sends request shapes; jordan to mark priority SIG rows.
[09:07] Jordan: thanks everyone. one last thing, the SIG had a question about incident response times and notification windows. can you summarize your SLA on incidents?
[09:17] Priya: our incident response for critical incidents is 15 minutes for initial ack, and we send notifications via email and pager. for enterprise we offer a faster pager cadence and runbooks. we'll include the incident playbook excerpt.
[09:31] Jordan: perfect. thanks.
[09:34] Alex: thanks all. we'll follow up with the attachments in 48-72 hours for the high-priority items.
[09:40] (call ends)

Notes: transcript has some speaker attribution errors (one attendee joined muted, one label unknown). references: SOC2 PDF link placeholder (to be attached), CAIQ mapping spreadsheet (to be shared), sample logs export (SFTP).
